summary.text: Lauren Pinkston, an independent from Columbia and former assistant professor at Lipscomb University, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Governor of Tennessee to Marsha Blackburn.
She began as a public school teacher, holds a doctorate from Clemson University and has started businesses employing survivors of human trafficking; it was her first campaign.

paragraphs.text: Pinkston describes herself as a seventh-generation Tennessean who grew up in Stantonville and is the mother of four.
She graduated from McNairy Central High School and earned a bachelor's degree in elementary education from Freed-Hardeman University in 2009.
She taught fourth grade in Memphis from 2009 to 2010 and in Greenwood, South Carolina, from 2010 to 2012, then earned a doctorate from Clemson University in 2019.
From 2020 to 2023 she was an assistant professor of business as mission at Lipscomb University.
Ballotpedia lists business development among her career experience.
Pinkston spent years in Thailand and Laos and started businesses employing survivors of human trafficking.
She filed to run for governor as an independent on February 13, 2026.
She received 1.2% of the vote to Marsha Blackburn's 45.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
